# Diffraction Reference Fixtures

This directory contains the machine-readable external-validation corpus for
Phase 22. The checked-in CSV is generated by the official EDB2 toolbox and is
covered by a Go regression test.

## Reference Provenance

The official NTNU EDB2 archive was downloaded and executed with GNU Octave
9.4.0 on 2026-08-09. Because the archive contains source but no output for this
case, [`generate_svensson_edb2.m`](generate_svensson_edb2.m) constructs the
manifest geometry and calls the official `EDB2wedge1st_fd` implementation.

| Artifact | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- |
| `EDB2toolbox_25April2015.zip` | `fd8dfcd13848817e116fe059fc25d3f07d462e9e070fd927dc6a2e1238b3af3d` |
| `EDBtoolbox_examples.zip` | `c3558bd7dbd52e0e2fdeac7aa39b1be5c1b3a47d743ab3b68999873b62bef3f0` |

Both archives are linked from Peter Svensson's official
[software page](https://ulfps.folk.ntnu.no/software/index.html) and are licensed
under GPL-3.0 according to that page. They are intentionally not vendored.

Octave's `quadgk` defaults to 650 intervals, which does not meet EDB2's requested
relative tolerance at 5 and 10 kHz for this 100 m edge. The generator raises
only `MaxIntervalCount` to 10000 in a temporary copy of the official driver. It
does not change the EDB2 integrand, relative tolerance, or returned quantity.
Two clean runs produced byte-identical CSV files. Runtime and artifact hashes
are recorded in [`reference-manifest.json`](reference-manifest.json).

## Reproduction Contract

The manifest fixes the repository's coordinate embedding, source/receiver
sweep, frequencies, output columns, and source artifacts. It canonicalizes the
rotation-invariant geometry described in Section 10.3 of the
[RAVEN dissertation](https://publications.rwth-aachen.de/record/50580/files/3875.pdf):
a 10-degree, 100 m finite wedge; source and 15 receivers at 10 m radius in the
edge-normal plane; receiver angles from -84 to +84 degrees in 12-degree steps.

To reproduce the fixture:

1. Download EDB2 from the official page and verify its SHA-256.
2. Add this directory to the MATLAB/Octave path and call
   `generate_svensson_edb2(toolbox_directory, output_csv)`. The checked-in file
   was produced with GNU Octave 9.4.0.
3. Run the generator twice and require byte-identical output.
4. Verify the generator and CSV hashes against the manifest.
5. Run `go test ./geometry` to compare the repository implementation against
   every reference row.

The fixture covers 50 Hz, 500 Hz, 5 kHz, and 10 kHz. The BTME acceptance
threshold is 0.5 dB below 12 kHz; all 60 receiver/frequency points pass. DAPDF
transition behavior is validated deterministically in the ray-tracing package;
a future external stochastic-energy corpus should still report the documented
low-frequency deep-shadow exception separately rather than hiding it in a mean.
